properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 11:40AM MDT until October 22 at 3:45PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Washington County in southwestern Utah...

* Until 345 PM MDT.

* At 1140 AM MDT, Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen across
the headwaters of Gould Wash from earlier thunderstorms which
created a large flood wave which continues to move through
Hurricane. Additional thunderstorms forming to the south and west
are expected to move back into this area exacerbating the flooding
within the next 30 to 45 minutes. Flash flooding is ongoing.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Gould Wash through Hurricane.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 3:45 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 3:45 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Riverton has issued a Red Flag
Warning, which is in effect from noon to 8 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS: Low Humidities...Strong Gusty Winds...and Wind Shift
with a Cold Front could cause erratic fire behavior.

* AFFECTED AREA:
In North Central WY...Fire Weather Zone 281.

* COUNTIES AFFECTED:
In North Central WY...Johnson.

* COLD FRONT: Moves in after 8 PM MDT Friday, with northerly 20 to
35 mph winds and gusts of 35 to 40 mph.

* WIND: Southwest 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* HUMIDITY: As low as 20 percent.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now....or will shortly. A combination of strong
winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

San Juan River At Farmington affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Farmington.

* WHEN...From this morning to Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 8.5 feet, Overbank flow is occurring from just below
the confluence of the Animas and San Juan Rivers at Farmington, and
continuing downriver through Shiprock. At this water level, the
fast flow can result in river bank erosion but otherwise minor
flood damage.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 5.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 7.2 feet
late tomorrow evening.
- Action stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.areaDesc: Emery, UT; Garfield, UT; Kane, UT; San Juan, UT; Sevier, UT; Wayne, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 11:28AM MDT until October 23 at 11:15AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Emery County in central Utah...
Southeastern Sevier County in central Utah...
Northwestern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...
Eastern Garfield County in southern Utah...
Northeastern Kane County in southern Utah...
Wayne County in southern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1115 AM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Prolonged and
widespread moderate to heavy rainfall will continue into tonight
before dissipating. This coupled with near-saturated soils will
allow rapidly increasing flows across all waterways within the
warned area, including all of Capitol Reef National Park, and the
San Rafael Swell south of I-70. Increasingly high flows are
expected in, but not limited to...the Fremont River, Muddy Creek,
the Dirty Devil and its tributaries, and slot canyons within the
San Rafael Reef.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1114 AM MDT, Capitol Reef National Park reported heavy rain in
the warned area due to thunderstorms. Flooding is already
occurring along the Fremont River which has closed Highway 24
between mile markers 80-86. Between 0.5 and 1.6 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1.5 inches are possible in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hanksville, Capitol Reef National Park, Torrey, Hite Marina,
Ticaboo, Teasdale, Bullfrog, Halls Crossing, Caineville, Goblin
Valley and Fruita.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

* WHAT...Northwest winds 15 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Coulee City, Bridgeport, Mansfield, Tonasket, Wilbur,
Nespelem, Omak, Oroville, Disautel Pass, Grand Coulee, Okanogan,
Ritzville, Brewster, Waterville, Harrington, Creston, Odessa, and
Badger Mountain Road.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 3 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
Motorists traveling along Highway 2 between Creston and Douglas
should take extra precaution and be prepared for strong cross
winds. Patchy blowing dust will be possible. New fire starts could
spread swiftly through dry fuel beds, especially in the afternoon
as humidity values lower near 20 percent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds will increase after midnight with peak
gusts between 3AM and 11AM. The axis of strongest winds will be
through the Okanogan Valley, across northwestern Douglas County and
into northern Grant and western Lincoln County between Creston and
Coulee City.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 22 at 10:44AM MDT until October 23 at 11:00PM MDT by NWS Rapid City SD
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 11 AM TO 11 PM MDT FRIDAY DUE TO
GUSTY WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR NORTHERN CAMPBELL, SOUTHERN
CAMPBELL, CROOK COUNTY PLAINS, AND WESTON COUNTY PLAINS...

.Warm temperatures, humidities as low as 13%, and southwest winds
gusting to 50 mph ahead of an approaching cold front will create
widespread critical fire weather conditions Friday afternoon through
Friday evening. Southwest winds increase over northeastern Wyoming
after 10 am Friday morning with sustained winds of 25 to 35 mph and
gusts of 40 to 50 mph through the afternoon. Winds will shift to the
northwest after midnight as the front moves through. While some
showers may accompany the front, not expecting any widespread wetting
rains.

The National Weather Service in Rapid City SD has issued a Red Flag
Warning in effect from 11 AM to 11 PM MDT Friday.

* TIMING...From 11 AM to 11 PM MDT Friday.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 13 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 22 at 8:43AM AKDT until October 25 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding expected. Water levels 5 to
7 feet above the normal high tide line expected for Hooper Bay.
Water levels 2 to 4 feet above the normal high tide line for
the rest of the Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast, particularly Hooper Bay.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Friday to 10 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...In Hooper Bay, beach property, and the lowest
buildings will be inundated. The access roads to the airstrip
and the larger parts of town will likely be inundated and access
to the airstrip will be cut off. Elsewhere along the Yukon Delta
Coastline, beach property and the lowest lying roads may be
threatened. Water levels will peak around midday Friday in
Hooper Bay then drop during the afternoon. Be aware that water
levels will remain high during each high tide into the weekend.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels peak with the high tides
Friday and then slowly decrease through the weekend. South to
southeast winds peak Friday with gusts up to 65 mph possible.
properties.instruction: Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property.

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Grand Junction CO has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Colorado...

San Juan River at Pagosa Springs affecting Archuleta County.

For the San Juan River...including Pagosa Springs...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Pagosa Springs.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 13.7 feet, Flooding of some residences near the river
around Pagosa Springs is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 8.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 8.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage late this
afternoon to 13.8 feet tomorrow morning. It will then fall below
flood stage tomorrow afternoon to 8.3 feet Saturday afternoon. It
will rise to 8.4 feet early Sunday morning. It will then fall
again and remain below flood stage.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/gjt.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight MDT.

properties.areaDesc: Imperial County Southwest; Imperial County West; Imperial Valley
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 22 at 7:36AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert
due to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...the Imperial Valley. Levels of particle pollution can vary
by time and location depending on emissions and local weather
conditions.

* WHEN...Thursday, October 22, 2026 until 11:00 PM.

* IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and
cause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung
disease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone
can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or
heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

To help minimize outdoor particle pollution levels:

* Carpool, telecommute, reduce trips, or take public
transportation
* Slow down if driving on dirt roads
* Stabilize loose soils
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.description:

Moenkopi Wash and the Little Colorado River.

* WHERE...Moenkopi Wash and the Little Colorado River from Cameron to
the Colorado River confluence.

is occurring. Further rises in the water levels of already flooded
creeks and normally dry washes. Deadly flooding over low-water
crossings.

remained above major flood stage. Elevated flow was also observed
on the Little Colorado River near Cameron. With additional heavy
rain expected, flooding is expected to continue.

Hamblin Wash, Begashibito Wash, Little Colorado River, Moenkopi
Wash, Bekihatso Wash, Fivemile Wash and Sheep Wash.

At 5:45am MST /6:45am MDT/ the stage was 36.38 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in
lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Moenkopi and Salt Trail Canyon.
- This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Blue Water Base Camp and Old Fish Camp Site.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 9:36AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the weekend. There
is potential for levels to approach Major Flood Stage next week,
after northeast winds increase again.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet Roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Thursday the stage was 3.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Thursday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1100 AM EDT.

Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.areaDesc: Garfield, UT; Kane, UT; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 6:16AM MDT until October 22 at 12:15PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...San Juan County in southeastern Utah...
Southwestern Garfield County in southern Utah...
Kane County in southern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of normally dry washes, slot canyons, rivers,
creeks, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is occurring.
Prolonged and widespread moderate to heavy rainfall will continue
trough this evening. This coupled with near-saturated soils will
allow rapidly increasing flows across all waterways within the
warned area, including all of the Glen Canyon National Recreation
Area. Increasingly high flows are expected in, but not limited
to...the Paria River, Wahweep Creek, Warm Creek, Last Chance Creek,
Croton Canyon, and the Escalante River Basin and tributaries. Many
backcountry roads within this area are expected to become
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 610 AM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen across the headwaters of the
Paria River, Escalante River, Wahweap Creek and other drainages
within the warned area. The Paria River at Highway 89 saw a peak
flow of nearly 2500 CFS overnight, while the Escalante River just
downstream from Escalante recorded a peak stage of 6 feet. These
flood waves will continue to move downstream through the morning
hours.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2.5 inches are possible
through this evening. This will result in continued high flows
and additional flooding of all rivers, streams and normally dry
washes within the warned area.
- Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, including the Escalante
region. Kodachrome State Park, Tropic, Cannonville, Escalante,
and Big Water
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks can become unstable and
unsafe.

* WHERE...Northern Bristol Bay Coast.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low lying areas. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Bering front arrives to the Southwest
Alaska coast Friday morning, bringing a prolonged period of
strong southerly winds towards the coast. These winds will
result in elevated water levels and high surf. This period of
winds will coincide with two tidal cycles and push water
levels 1.0 to 2.0 feet above the normal highest tide line.

as winds decrease, alleviating coastal concerns.

due to 35 to 50 mph winds with gusts up to 75 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...8 AM Friday through 1 AM Saturday, particularly around
high tides near 10 AM and 10 PM Friday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely scenario is for water
levels to be 2.0 to 3.0 ft above the normal high tide line,
which would be similar to the water levels during the August
18 2024 storm. While unlikely, the worst case scenario for

normal high tide line, while the worst case for Kwigillingok
is 4.0 to 5.0 feet above the normal high tide line. We are
closely monitoring this storm. In the meantime, please have a
plan in place.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...In Delaware, Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches. In
New Jersey, Ocean and Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.areaDesc: Central Mountains; Castle Country; San Rafael Swell; Lower Washington County; Zion National Park; Southern Mountains; Upper Sevier River Valleys; Bryce Canyon Country; South Central Utah; Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity; Western Canyonlands; Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 2:45AM MDT until October 23 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, San Rafael Swell, Bryce Canyon Country,
Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation
Area/Lake Powell, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper
Sevier River Valleys, Western Canyonlands, Lower Washington County
and Zion National Park.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A late season surge of tropical moisture will bring widespread
moderate to at times heavy rainfall across much of southern Utah
through Thursday. Local rainfall totals in excess of 3 inches are
expected through Thursday evening.
- All normally dry washes, small streams and mainstem rivers will
see elevated flows from this excessive rainfall, with periods of
heavier rainfall resulting in flash flooding. Backcountry roads
may become impassable due to flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

People in the backcountry should ensure they have alternative routes
available in case their primary route becomes impassable.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Outer Banks
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 22 at 4:03AM EDT until October 22 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1 to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 8 to 10 feet in the surf zone. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, dangerous rip currents and large breaking waves
expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT this
evening. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT this
morning through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some roads and
low lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and
homes adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow
flooding. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore
break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom
causing neck and back injuries.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, up to 2 to 4 ft of
inundation above ground level in low- lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the
Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents and large
breaking waves expected in the surf zone.

resulting in a low threat of property damage. Flooding will

conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep
even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

into the bottom causing neck and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...NC-12 between the Basnight Bridge and
Rodanthe remains closed. Significant ocean overwash impacts are
expected to continue for vulnerable oceanside areas today,
especially around high tide.

water of unknown depth.

conditions.

properties.description:

continue to be possible over the Wapiti Fire burn scar.

* WHERE...A portion of central Idaho, including the following area,
Sawtooth/Stanley Basin.

* WHEN...From this evening through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Wapiti Fire burn scar is expected
during the period of the watch. Anyone in or near the Wapiti burn
scar should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the
Wapiti burn scar. Be sure to stay up to date with information from
local authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding and
debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the Wapiti Fire burn scar, which may lead to flash
flooding and debris flows.

Cape Horn Area and Banner Summit.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 12:24AM MDT until October 23 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of western, central, and north-central New Mexico,
mainly along and west of the Continental Divide.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A potent Pacific storm system will continue to draw deep moisture
over western New Mexico generating widespread showers and
thunderstorms. Some of the fast moving thunderstorms will produce
locally heavy rain at rates over 1 inch per hour, and storms will
train in succession over some locations repeatedly increasing the
risk of flash flooding. Additional rain amounts for the remainder
of tonight through late Thursday night will generally range from
0.25 inch to 1 inch, with locally higher totals up to 3 inches.
- This includes Farmington, Gallup, Zuni Pueblo, and portions of
Navajo Nation.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 22 at 12:57AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
Relative humidity will fall below 25 percent again this afternoon
across northeast Georgia. Given the dry vegetation and low fine
fuel moisture, outdoor fires will be able to spread quickly once
started, increasing the danger of wildfires.

Please refer to your local burn permitting authority on whether
you can burn today. If you do burn, use extreme caution since
fires can quickly get out of hand under these conditions.

properties.description:

are possible over the Crooked burn scar and Wapiti burn scar. Total
rainfall up to 1 inch is possible on the burn scars.

* WHERE...Wapiti and Crooked burn scars in southwest Idaho.

* WHEN...From Thursday evening through Friday morning.

debris flow. Be sure to stay up to date with information from local
authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding or debris
flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars.

rainfall over the Crooked and Wapiti burn scar, which may lead to
flash flooding and debris flows.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 21 at 11:58PM EDT until October 24 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 8 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 PM EDT
Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Saturday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 21 at 8:35PM EDT until October 24 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...The beaches of Volusia, Brevard, Indian River, Saint
Lucie, and Martin Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 21 at 12:35PM CDT by NWS Jackson MS
properties.description:
According to local forestry agencies and the U.S. Forest Service,
recent longstanding drought conditions have led to extremely dry
fuels, making outdoor burning increasingly hazardous. Conditions
are such that a spark from equipment, the heat from a catalytic
converter, or any heat source could start a grass or brush fire.
The combination of dry fine fuels, such as grass, and low relative
humidity will continue to result elevated fire danger across the
region this week.

Minimum relative humidity values will range from upper teens to
below 30 percent during the daytime hours the next couple of days,
supporting increased fire danger given the longstanding drought
conditions and extremely dry and wildfire prone fuels. 20ft winds
remain light during this timeframe.

These extremely dry conditions will support the spread of
wildfires, even with light winds. Outdoor burning and activities
that involve open sparks or flames are discouraged and extra
caution is advised with any open burning. Please report all
wildfires to local law enforcement as soon as possible.

Numerous counties and parishes are under local burn bans at the
present time. Fires place local forestry agencies, fire departments,
and other fire control agencies in life threatening situations,
and can endanger communities. Please use caution and help prevent
forest and grass fires.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 21 at 5:53AM MST until October 22 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An upper-level trough will bring a deep surge of subtropical and
tropical moisture into our region. Showers and thunderstorms will
develop across much of northern and central Arizona early
Wednesday morning and continue through Thursday evening. Stronger
thunderstorms will bring threats of Flash Flooding, while more
prolonged rainfall could lead to elevated flow in streams,
rivers, and washes.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 19 at 12:31PM PDT until October 23 at 3:00AM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to
elevated surf of 3 to 6 feet expected.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor beach erosion and tidal overflows may
occur across south-facing beaches especially along the Malibu
Coast and in the Long Beach area.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.
